questions.text: The potential difference between points lying on the same field line of a uniform electric field, 0.03 m apart, is 12 V. Find the potential difference between points on the same field line that are 15 cm apart.
The electric field strength in a parallel-plate capacitor is 30 kV/m. The potential difference between the plates is 300 V. What is the distance between the capacitor plates (in mm)?
Two parallel metal plates in vacuum, 0.1 m apart, are charged to a potential difference of 1 kV. What force acts on a 100 µC charge placed between the plates?

A dust particle of mass $4.8 \cdot 10^{-12}$ kg is in equilibrium between the horizontal plates of a parallel-plate capacitor. If the voltage across the capacitor is 3000 V and the distance between the plates is 2 cm, how many times greater is the charge of the dust particle than the charge of an electron? ($e=1.6 \cdot 10^{-19}$ C, $g=10 \, m/s^2$).

A charged ball is suspended on a plastic spring between the horizontal plates of a parallel-plate capacitor. When the capacitor is connected to a 500 V voltage source, the spring stretches by an additional 1 cm. Find the charge of the ball (in µC) if the spring constant is 10 N/m and the distance between the capacitor plates is 20 cm.

A negatively charged dust particle of mass $10^{-9}$ g is in equilibrium inside a parallel-plate capacitor. A voltage of 500 V is applied to the capacitor. By how many volts must the potential difference be changed so that the particle stays in equilibrium after 500 electrons have left it? ($d=5$ mm).

A charged ball hangs between the plates of a parallel-plate capacitor at a distance of 10 cm from the lower plate ($U=400$ V). If the potential difference is instantly reduced to 200 V, after what time (in ms) will the ball fall onto the lower plate?

An electron entered the field of a parallel-plate capacitor along the field lines and lost its speed over a distance of 0.003 m. At what distance (in mm) will it stop if the initial speed of the electron and the voltage across the capacitor are both reduced by a factor of 3?

Electrons that gained speed by passing through a potential difference of 5 kV enter a parallel-plate capacitor at the midpoint (parallel to the plates). What is the smallest voltage needed to keep the electrons from leaving the capacitor? ($L=5$ cm, $d=1$ cm).
At two vertices of an equilateral triangle with side 30 cm there are charges of 50 nC each. Find the potential at the third vertex (in kV).
At two opposite vertices of a square with side 30 cm there are charges of 200 nC each. Find the potential at the other two vertices of the square (in kV).
Charges of 1, 2 and 3 nC are located at the vertices of a right triangle. If the length of the hypotenuse is 20 cm, what is the potential at its midpoint? ($k=9 \cdot 10^9$).
Charges of 3, 5 and –2 nC are located at three vertices of a regular tetrahedron with edge 30 cm. Find the potential at the fourth vertex.
Charges of 1 nC each are located at three vertices of a regular hexagon with side 27 cm, and charges of 2 nC each at the other three. Find the potential at the center of the hexagon.
A charge of 4 nC is distributed along a thin ring of radius 6 cm. Find the potential of the field at a point on the axis of the ring, 8 cm from its center.
A charge of 4 nC is distributed over the surface of a sphere of radius 30 cm. What is the potential at the center of the sphere?
A small ball with a negative charge of –5 nC is located at the center of a sphere with a positive charge of 10 nC. Find the potential at a point outside the sphere, 9 cm from its center.
What work (in µJ) does the field do in moving a charge of 2 nC from one point of the field to another?⏎The potential difference between the points is $\Delta \varphi = 500$ V.
What work (in µJ) is done in moving a charge of 8 µC from a point of the field with a potential of 20 V to a point with a potential of 12 V?
The work done in moving a charge of 130 nC from infinity to some point of the field is 65 µJ. Find the potential (V) of that point.
Moving a charge of 10 nC from infinity to a point 20 cm from the surface of a charged ball required 0.5 µJ of work. ($R=4$ cm). Find the potential at the surface of the ball.
When a negative charge was moved toward a fixed positive charge, the field did 9 J of work and the distance was halved. What work (J) was done over the first half of this path?
